tools.name: show_flight_options
tools.title: Show flight options
tools.description: Searches flights and returns them as an interactive A2UI surface the user can pick from, instead of a list of text. Use whenever the user is choosing a flight.

origin.description: Departure airport code. Required — the trip is not priced without one.

surface.description: Where this surface will be placed. 'inline' (default) answers the current message; 'sidebar' is a persistent panel of controls; 'home' is a standing summary. It changes what is composed, not just where it goes.

tools.name: show_hotel_options
tools.title: Show places to stay
tools.description: Searches stays and returns them as A2UI hotel cards with rating, neighbourhood and nightly rate.

surface.description: Where this surface will be placed. 'inline' (default) answers the current message; 'sidebar' is a persistent panel of controls; 'home' is a standing summary. It changes what is composed, not just where it goes.

tools.name: show_trip_controls
tools.title: Show trip controls (sidebar)
tools.description: Returns the sidebar flow: a panel of controls for the trip as a whole — dates, party size, budget, stop preference — with one commit action. Use it when the user wants to *adjust* the trip rather than discuss it. The panel replaces itself each time; it is not a feed.

tools.name: show_itinerary
tools.title: Show a day-by-day itinerary
tools.description: Builds a day-by-day plan for a destination from its real highlights and returns it as an A2UI itinerary the user can tap through.

surface.description: Where this surface will be placed. 'inline' (default) answers the current message; 'sidebar' is a persistent panel of controls; 'home' is a standing summary. It changes what is composed, not just where it goes.

tools.name: show_trip_dashboard
tools.title: Show a trip dashboard
tools.description: Returns a generated dashboard for a trip: days remaining, budget used, forecast and a map of what is planned. Use for "how is my trip looking" questions.

tools.name: show_price_summary
tools.title: Show what a trip costs
tools.description: Returns an itemised cost breakdown and total as an A2UI price summary.

surface.description: Where this surface will be placed. 'inline' (default) answers the current message; 'sidebar' is a persistent panel of controls; 'home' is a standing summary. It changes what is composed, not just where it goes.

tools.name: get_a2ui_component_reference
tools.title: Read the component catalog
tools.description: Returns the full A2UI Express output contract: the grammar, the streaming rules, and the positional signature of every component and function in the travel catalog — flight and hotel cards, itinerary days, maps, price summaries, stat tiles, sliders, pickers, and the layout primitives. Call this once before render_a2ui_express, then compose whatever interface the conversation actually needs. Costs one call and makes every layout possible rather than the six this server hard-codes.

tools.name: render_a2ui_express
tools.title: Compose a custom interface
tools.description: Compiles A2UI Express you have written into a live interface, rendered by the same React component library as every other tool here. This is the general case and the other tools are shortcuts: use it whenever the layout you want is not one of them — a comparison table of three hotels next to a budget meter, a packing checklist, a single decision card. Call get_a2ui_component_reference first for the grammar and the signatures. Compile errors come back naming exactly what was wrong, so a second attempt can fix it.

source.description: A2UI Express source. Declare components in order and finish with `root = …`; sentinel tags are optional, the compiler strips them.

surfaceId.description: Surface id to draw into. Defaults to "mcp".

tools.name: export_a2ui_app
tools.description: Compiles A2UI Express into a **standalone HTML page** with the renderer baked into it — the same React components every other tool here draws with, and nothing to fetch. Use it when your host can show generated HTML but does not render MCP Apps: write the result to a file and open or publish it, and the interface appears. Sandboxed HTML usually may only load scripts from a short list of CDNs, so a page that *links* this renderer draws nothing; this one carries it. The page is about 250 kB, which is the renderer — prefer render_a2ui_express when the host draws MCP Apps itself.

source.description: A2UI Express source, exactly as render_a2ui_express takes it.

surfaceId.description: Surface id to draw into. Defaults to "mcp".
